page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a high-density GPU-accelerated server designed for intensive computational workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this KVM-based virtual machine features 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processors running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 960.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, delivering a combined total of 320 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. Notably, this instance does not include local storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data.

Benchmark data highlights the server's capabilities in parallel processing and memory throughput. The system achieves a PassMark CPU score of 85,426.66 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance of 96,293.69, reflecting strong multi-threaded compute capacity. Memory performance is characterized by a top-tier read-only small block bandwidth of 7,649.82 GB/sec and a large block write bandwidth of 135.84 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM inference with a small 135M model, processing 10,308.98 tokens per second during prompt processing and 377.14 tokens per second during text generation.

From a resource-density perspective, the server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for massive parallel workloads by combining substantial system memory with four enterprise-grade GPUs on a shared CPU allocation model. However, the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage represent key architectural tradeoffs that require careful workload planning. This server is highly suited for large-scale machine learning, deep learning model training, LLM inference, high-performance computing, and complex data science tasks that leverage GPU acceleration and massive memory footprints.
